I'm 65 years old now, been farming these 2 mu in Quzhou for 45 years, and it's just me since my wife passed. I finished middle school, so I can read the numbers on fertilizer bags and I listen when the extension technician comes by, but at the end of the day I trust what my own eyes have seen season after season. My land is small, only 2 mu, so every yuan I spend has to count — I can't afford to waste inputs, but I also can't afford a bad year because this is all the land I have.

It's early spring now and my winter wheat is greening up. I planted an improved wheat variety last October — probably something like Shimai 22 that I bought from the seed shop in town. Back then I spread about 100 jin of compound fertilizer per mu as basal and did rotary tillage. Now I need to topdress. I will put down about 25 jin of urea per mu when the wheat turns green at jointing. That gives me roughly 20 kg of nitrogen per mu in total, plus about 18 kg of phosphorus and 5 kg of potassium from the compound. I will irrigate three times this wheat season: once at green-up, once at jointing, and once at grain filling. The electricity bill for pumping adds up, but three irrigations is what I've always done and it keeps the yield safe. I'll spray twice for pesticides — once for weeds and once for fungus or aphids if they show up at heading. I expect about 900 jin per mu, maybe a bit more if the weather stays good.

For the summer maize, I'll plant right after wheat harvest in early June. I use a hybrid variety like Nongda 372 — everyone around here uses hybrids now, there's no point going back to old seed. I'll do no-tillage planting because I'm alone and there's barely a week between wheat harvest and maize sowing; I don't have the labor or time to plow. I'll put down about 90 jin of compound fertilizer per mu at planting — that's roughly 20 kg nitrogen, 5 kg phosphorus, and 5 kg potassium per mu. I plan to irrigate twice if the summer is dry, usually once at the big trumpet stage and once at flowering. Two pesticide sprays: herbicide right after sowing, and insecticide later if I see armyworms. If things go normally, I should get about 950 jin per mu of maize.
